contributions.reason: The first present ID field controls mapping even when non-string; validation independently permits a later string. Five live production priority vectors match.
Non-object SSE acceptance is not the pinned behavior; frozen metadata kernel rejects non-objects and the Rust wrapper panics.

The catch preserves events before an observer exception but its non-object error expectation is not release parity. The live synthetic release client times out for null, array and text-then-null in one event.

Raw-key matching bypasses the production Serde decode/reserialize boundary. Escaped keys and decoded duplicate priority regress. Parent replay: 3004 cases, 557 mismatches against the source-derived production model; live buffered and SSE production regressions protect decoded handling.
Historical raw transform fallback is preceded by full request format validation. Live production missing/non-string types return 502 with zero POSTs; the patch would incorrectly accept them.
